{"decision":"Recorded as BRAINSTORMING, not as a proposal. Distinct from dec:idea-should-reflow2-serve-a-root-cause-analysis-method, which DECIDED that reflow2 serves the method; this asks when its USE becomes automatic. Anthony, 2026-09-06, in his words: 'I now use the /root-cause skill a lot and it seems to really drive the agent to identifying the real cause and not treating a symptom or fixing the wrong thing. In all my projects now, I've made design rules that basically say, when you identify an issue, run /root-cause. That being said, I'd like to make the use of /root-cause more automatic by the agent when it finds an issue in implementing/creating design artifacts or in its testing. I know there is probably some caveats about which types of issues the /root-cause should be run on, so might not be a blanket rule to always run /root-cause.'

THE OPTIONS, as they separate:
(a) A BLANKET RULE — every failure met while building or testing runs the skill. Simplest to state; no judgement at the moment of failure.
(b) TRIGGER ON THE SKILL'S OWN TELL — not 'something failed' but 'I am about to write down a CAUSE'. The skill's own text says this is the moment ('that's odd', 'it must be X', 'that explains it'), and that its author missed it on a quiet number and produced four wrong causes. Failures whose remedy is IN the error text (a compile error naming the line; a refusal that names the legal values; an unknown-field refusal that lists the fields) never reach a cause — you read, fix, move on — and are exempt by construction.
(c) A TIERED RULE — ALWAYS run step ② (search the raw error text for a recorded cause; measured cold at 0.08 s) on ANY failure, and proceed to ③–⑤ only when no precedent is found OR when you have formed an explanation. Step ② alone would have prevented both measured failures on this project: the 11-occurrence error of 2026-08-22 whose cause sat in the graph, and the 2026-09-06 re-fix of an already-fixed defect.

WHICH ISSUES (the caveat Anthony named), as a first cut for him to correct: RUN IT on an unpredicted test failure; a measurement or count you cannot account for; a field-reported defect (already the rule); a surprise in your own build ('why did that pass/fail'); and any sentence containing 'because' before a measurement was taken. DO NOT run the full skill on: an error whose remedy is stated in the error itself; a known-class friction whose cause is already recorded (but COUNT the recurrence — five argument-shape refusals in one triage on 2026-09-05 were evidence, not five investigations); a typo. Whether 'known class' is judged by the agent or by step ②'s search is exactly the (b)-vs-(c) difference.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — should /root-cause run automatically when the agent meets an issue while building or testing, and on WHICH kinds of issue? (Anthony: 'probably some caveats … might not be a blanket rule')","rationale":"COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the options rather than used to kill them. Against (a): the skill 'costs real time', and run on every trivial refusal it becomes a ritual — the 2026-09-05 triage met five argument-shape refusals in an hour; five full investigations would have been absurd, and a step performed ritually stops being performed at all (the skill's own warning: 'if you find yourself agreeing with these steps rather than doing them, the skill has already failed'). Against the EXEMPTIONS in (b) and (c): the skill's own author-case says 'this one is obvious' is the case to run it on, not skip it for — an exemption list is a loophole with a name, and the overconfident-fix case Anthony described (fact:surfacing-a-known-cause-is-cheap-and-reaches-the-wrong-half) produces NO failing command at all, so any trigger keyed on failures misses the half he most wants. That is why (b) keys on the CAUSE moment, not the failure. For (c): it is the cheapest honest floor — 0.08 s per failure, and it catches the recorded-cause class mechanically — but it does not reach the abstract third of defect facts that no error string matches (68 of 192 measured). A RANKING IS A FINDING, NOT A DECISION: (c) as the floor, (b) as the rule of judgement above it, (a) rejected as ritual. Anthony rules; the mechanism by which any of these becomes automatic is the sibling question dec:idea-how-does-root-cause-become-automatic-rule-hook-detector-or-composition.","status":"proposed"}
